name: universal-builder
//productName: Electron reads this for app.getName(), which is what names the menu bar and the userData folder. Without it both fall back to `name` and the app calls itself universal-builder.
description: Universal Builder -- one application replacing AERS Autobuilder v2.5 and the AERS-Autobuilder beta.
author: Charles Pollaers

scripts.//build: Package the bootstrap. Almost nothing changes here -- the .app is a loader, and day-to-day changes ship through publish:external instead.
scripts.test: npm run test:invariants --silent && npm run test:snapshots --silent
scripts.//test:invariants: What correct means, asserted against the decisions rather than against today's output. These never drift and are never waived -- publishing stops dead on one.
scripts.test:invariants: node tests/update.js && node tests/precedence.js && node tests/palette.js && node tests/brief-errors.js
scripts.//test:snapshots: What the engine currently produces. These move whenever the library is edited, which is most days; the suites tell accounted-for drift from an unexplained change. See docs/adr/0006-snapshots-record-their-inputs.md.
scripts.//test:strict: The snapshots with drift treated as failure too -- for checking the baselines are current before a commit.
scripts.//test:precedence: Asserts ADR 0005's layer order end to end, by building a brief that puts the layers in conflict. Unlike the golden files it says what should happen rather than what does.
scripts.//test:palette: Asserts that setPalettes() does not overrule the layers that ran before it. Its module-directed button cases all failed until settingsOf() landed.
scripts.//test:accept: Re-record both snapshot suites and their input manifests. Review the diff and commit it -- that commit is the record of what a change did to real output.
scripts.//publish:external: Push external/ to the shared folder every installed app reads from. Runs the golden tests first and refuses to publish on an unexpected diff. Always run publish:external:dry first.

//build-config: external/ is deliberately NOT packaged -- see docs/adr/0001-engine-runs-outside-the-app-bundle.md. node_modules IS, because the external tree resolves its packages from the app's copy over NODE_PATH.
